en.title: D
en.summary: The letter name is De, as in the word Danke.

sections.title: The letter De
paragraphs: You name this letter (De) /deː/. Its main sound is a voiced consonant, heard in (Danke) /ˈdaŋkə/, which means thank you. Voiced means your voice is on. Touch your throat and you feel it shake. This letter has two sounds.

sections.title: Mouth and voice
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air for a moment, then release it while turning your voice on. For the second sound, keep the same mouth position. Release the air without turning your voice on. Put a hand on your throat to feel the voice stop.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: At the beginning of words or syllables, this letter makes its voiced sound as in (oder) /ˈoːdɐ/. At the end of a syllable or word, it becomes voiceless. You say it as a clean stop, heard in (Bad) /baːt/ and (und) /ʊnt/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not soften the ending into the soft voice of bed. Keep the final sound crisp, exactly like the t in cat. Release the air with a clear, sharp stop.
